problems.claim: WTP: ADAudit Plus from $595/yr
problems.issue: The ManageEngine page shows cheaper plans than $595: $245/year for 100 workstations and $495/year for 2 Windows file servers. $595 is the 2-domain-controller Standard plan, not the starting price.

problems.claim: Vendor Anchore Enterprise: pricing not public (pricing page lists deployment options only, no prices)
problems.issue: The cited source is anchore.com/platform/. It says nothing about pricing or a pricing page, so it does not support the pricing claim.

problems.claim: Vendor Pillar Security (Pillar for AI Coding Agents): discovers local coding agents, scans permissions/MCP configs; AWS Marketplace $175,000/12 months
problems.issue: The cited AWS listing describes the general Pillar Security Platform (AI apps, agents, MCP, red teaming, guardrails). It does not mention coding agents or local agent discovery. The $175,000/12 months is for the whole platform, not a coding-agent product.

problems.claim: Vendor Vanta: no rate card on site; Essentials $14,000 / Plus $21,500 / Professional $23,000 (1-20 employees); audit extra
problems.issue: The AWS prices are correct. But the same listing says to 'preview pricing for 1-20 employees and more at vanta.com/pricing', which contradicts 'no rate card on site'. Nothing on the page says the audit costs extra.

problems.claim: WTP: Large enterprises spend ~$2.5M/yr on logging and 67% say cost outweighs value
problems.issue: Dynatrace gives ~$2.5M as the average annual spend of its survey respondents. It does not describe them as large enterprises. The 67% figure is supported.

problems.claim: WTP: Devolutions lists packages at $48-650/user/year
problems.issue: The $650 is a struck-through list price. The current price of that top package is $325, so the published range is $48-$325 per user per year.

problems.claim: Vendor GitHub Code Security: basic Dependabot included with GitHub
problems.issue: The cited changelog gives only Code Security at $30 per active committer per month, which includes Dependabot features. It does not say basic Dependabot is free or included with GitHub.

problems.claim: Vendor Vanta: compliance automation with NIS2 task templates and CMMC/NIST 800-171 mappings
problems.issue: The cited vanta.com/products/cmmc page covers CMMC, NIST 800-171/172, SSP and POA&M only. It does not mention NIS2.

problems.claim: WTP: NIS2-Autopilot EUR 249-799/mo
problems.issue: The cited Capterra page (plain and rendered fetch) gives only a starting price of EUR 249 per month, flat rate. There is no EUR 799 figure.

problems.claim: Vendor Fortinet FortiGate + FortiGuard/FortiCare: NGFW appliances with annual FortiGuard subscriptions and FortiCare support; segment SMB to enterprise, public sector
problems.issue: The cited page is a Gartner Magic Quadrant landing page about enterprise networks. It does not mention FortiGuard or FortiCare subscriptions, SMB or public-sector buyers.

problems.claim: Vendor Check Point Quantum (Spark to 16000+): Quantum gateways with SandBlast/threat-prevention subscriptions; segment mid-market and enterprise, public sector
problems.issue: The cited blog post covers the Hybrid Mesh Firewall MQ leadership for 'enterprises'. It does not mention Quantum, Spark, 16000+, SandBlast, subscriptions, mid-market or public sector.

problems.claim: WTP: paid backup and file-security products with public per-device and per-server prices (Acronis, Veeam, ManageEngine) sell widely
problems.issue: None of the WTP sources is a ManageEngine page, so the ManageEngine part has no source. No source shows that these products 'sell widely'.

problems.claim: WTP: buyers still file issues about missing policy-as-code control of paid Defender plans
problems.issue: The cited GitHub issue #735 is from May 2023, and its author closed it. The author found the setting can be applied when the deployment is part of a policy. The issue does not show a current, unresolved complaint.

problems.claim: Vendor Anchore Enterprise: imports SPDX and CycloneDX 1.0-1.6 SBOMs
problems.issue: The cited AWS Marketplace listing does not mention SPDX, CycloneDX or any format versions. The prices ($34,500 Cloud Image, $50,000 Helm) are supported.

problems.claim: Vendor Fairwinds Insights: Kubernetes policy management and admission control using Polaris, OPA and Kyverno
problems.issue: The cited pricing page lists only a 'Kubernetes Policy Management' module. It does not mention Polaris, OPA, Kyverno or admission control.

problems.claim: Vendor secunet SINA Workstation S: BSI-approved Lenovo ThinkPad bundle, sold via government framework contracts; segment federal government, Bundeswehr, defence industry
problems.issue: The cited BSI page describes a notebook hardware/software bundle with VPN, disk encryption and parallel guest OSes, for the federal administration. It does not mention Lenovo ThinkPad, framework contracts, the Bundeswehr or the defence industry.

problems.claim: WTP: state police tendering up to 6,000 approved clients
problems.issue: The Saarland police TED notice requires the VPN solution to scale to up to 6,000 endpoints. That is a scalability requirement, not an order for 6,000 clients.

problems.claim: Vendor RadarFirst: incident decisioning incl. SEC materiality; segment enterprise
problems.issue: The cited Capterra page lists typical users as freelancers, small businesses, mid-size businesses and enterprises. It does not mention SEC materiality. 'Contact vendor' pricing is supported.

problems.claim: WTP: SMB NIS2 platforms start ~EUR 10,000
problems.issue: The only source is SECJUR's own blog, stating its own product costs 'ab 10.000 Euro' for the German Mittelstand. It is one vendor's self-reported price, not evidence of where SMB NIS2 platforms in general start.

problems.claim: Vendor Semgrep Supply Chain: Team $30 per contributor/month (some Semgrep pages show $40)
problems.issue: The cited semgrep.dev/pricing page shows $30/month/contributor for Supply Chain and has no $40 figure.
